title: Introduce KMS consent oracle and audit-sequencer to ensure residency-consent consistency
author: Nora Patel
description:
Motivation: customers in regulated regions require per-request consent checks to ensure KMS usage and data residency are aligned with tenant preferences and policy. This PR introduces a small, auditable service (the 'KMS consent oracle') plus an in-path audit sequencer that ensures every request that touches a cross-region or fallback KMS publishes a signed 'consent attestation' and an ordered audit record. Design summary: 1) Consent Oracle: a read-through service consulted by the request-authorizer. It resolves tenant consent profiles, residency constraints, and approved KMS provider lists, returning a canonical consent token. 2) Audit Sequencer: a lightweight sequencer that attaches monotonically increasing audit sequence IDs per-tenant-request-window, emits signed audit envelopes to the audit-log-forwarder, and rejects requests where attestation was not captured. 3) KMS Fallback Policy: a policy engine that allows fallback to approved alternate KMS providers only when explicit consent and policy scope permit it; otherwise the request is denied with clear error codes for clients. Implementation notes: service implemented in go/services/kmsconsent; auth hook added to gateway/authz to consult oracle during preflight; audit sequencer middleware added to runtime/handler and to the private installer flow for on-prem parity. Backwards compatibility: the oracle returns a v1 token; older runtimes will treat missing token as 'unknown' and will be denied by default unless the tenant has an explicit legacy-allow flag. Checklist: - [x] implement oracle service with in-memory cache and Redis backing - [x] add policy rules and unit coverage - [x] add sequencer middleware and integration tests - [x] wire signed audit envelopes into audit-forwarder - [x] add Linear tasks and update runbook - [x] update API docs and console messaging - [x] add migration to populate default consent profiles Testing and validation: local unit tests (go test) and integration tests using the perf-canary harness; added a synthetic scenario that simulates a primary KMS outage to validate fallback behavior and audit sequencing. Load testing: sequencer adds ~0.4ms median overhead in our canary workload at 12k RPS; cache hit paths reduce oracle resolution to sub-ms. Rollout plan: canary in staging behind a feature flag (security.kms_consent=true) for 48h, then staged rollout to 5% of requests on main cluster for 72h, monitor audit delivery (SLO: 99.99% delivery within 60s) and error rate. If errors or missing attestations exceed thresholds, auto-roll back. Ops runbook and Linear tasks are linked to ENG-9742. Why this is different: instead of embedding consent checks into the KMS allocator itself, the oracle centralizes consent resolution and makes attestations first-class auditables so compliance teams can prove per-request consent decisions. Introduces opt-in feature flag and staged rollout plan." Security rationale: improves our ability to produce immutable per-request consent proof for audits, reduces silent fallback risk, centralizes policy interpretation. Rollback plan: disable feature flag and remove gateway hook; sequencer will stop emitting new envelopes but audit-forwarder will continue to accept queued envelopes until drained. release_notes: Adds a tenant-level consent oracle and audit sequencer to require signed consent attestations for cross-region or fallback KMS usage; introduces an opt-in feature flag and staged rollout.
testing: Unit tests for oracle and policy parser; integration tests in tests/integration/kms_consent_test.go; perf-canary run validated latency impact; manual canary in staging prior to rollout.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged canary (48h) -> 5% traffic for 72h -> increase to 25% -> global if no issues. Monitoring: audit delivery SLO, error rate, sequencer latency.
security_rationale: Centralizes consent logic to produce auditable tokens and signed envelopes, preventing silent KMS fallbacks and giving compliance teams per-request attestation proof.
